subject: Post-demo: OrbitHealth data handling follow-ups & proposed next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Morales <anna@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today

Hi Anna — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Objective: use Redwood to power clinician notes enhancement and triage suggestions, with PHI present in prompts.
- Primary concerns you raised: PII handling, data residency (EU for pilot), and debug/logging exposure for troubleshooting.
- Ask: you requested an option where request payloads are not retained (0-retention) for production PHI, with short-term ephemeral logging only for debugging during onboarding.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I’ll surface the exact data handling options and a pragmatic tradeoff we can operationalize for pilot (SLA + purge confirmation).
2) If OrbitHealth is comfortable with an agreed short debug window, we can scope a pilot SOW and template redline.
3) Please confirm who on your side should receive the legal/privacy materials (I see Jane from legal on the thread).

Can you confirm timeline expectations from OrbitHealth for the pilot (start window) and whether EU residency is a hard requirement for the initial pilot or only for production?

Thanks — I’ll loop in Aditya (privacy) and Laura (AE) with a concrete proposal.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0123

--
Redwood Inference

From: Anna Morales <anna@orbithealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jane Liu <jane.liu@orbithealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- EU residency: for pilot, we can tolerate US-hosted infra as long as PHI is explicitly not persisted outside our controlled environment. Production will require EU residency, but pilot could be in us-east if we have contractual guarantees on retention and encryption.
- 0-retention ask: ideally, request payloads with PHI are never written to persistent logs. We understand debug traces are necessary for onboarding, so we could accept ephemeral debug logs with a maximum retention window. What we need is a concrete maximum (in hours/days) and an automated purge plus confirmation.
- Access & audit: only our security team + named Redwood ops should be able to access debug logs. We will request audit entries showing who accessed what and when.

Jane (cc) — we’ll need Redwood’s SOC2 snapshot and a short privacy summary for our security review.

If Redwood can propose a binding short-window compromise for debug logs (and a clear purge confirmation process), we can move to SOW drafting next week.

—Anna
CTO, OrbitHealth

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: OrbitHealth clarifications — need recommended approach

Team — forwarding Anna’s reply (below). Can you advise on the tightest practical option we can offer for OrbitHealth that balances debugging needs and their 0-retention requirement for PHI? Specifically: 

- Can we promise request-body-level 0-retention (never written to disk) while keeping very short-lived ephemeral debug traces (KV/cache & pipeline metadata) for up to X hours?
- What does the purge confirmation process look like (time to confirm, artifact of purge)?
- For EU residency: what’s our standard timeline & cost to spin up EU-only tenant for production?

Laura — can you own next steps with Anna once we have the proposal? I’ll include the privacy docs we can share.

Thanks,
Sean

> On Wed, Oct 21, 2026 at 4:03 PM Anna Morales <anna@orbithealth.com> wrote:
> > Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:...

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: RE: OrbitHealth clarifications — recommended approach and proposed compromise

Hi team — thanks for pulling this together. Proposed pragmatic approach we can commit to for a pilot, with implementation notes: 

1) Scope: production behavior = 0-retention for full request payloads containing PHI. No request bodies written to persistent logs or long-term storage.

2) Debug window: we can offer an "Ephemeral Debug Window" of up to 72 hours (3 days) for operational traces and KV/cache artifacts used only for troubleshooting during onboarding. These debug artifacts are stored encrypted, access-controlled, and are automatically purged after the window. Purge is triggered by TTL enforcement and background job; we can provide a purge certificate (hash + timestamp) signed by our internal logging service when the job completes.

3) Access & audit: debug artifacts are accessible only to:
   - Named OrbitHealth identities (we will collect user emails for access grants)
   - Redwood ops on an as-needed basis (with justification workflow)
   All accesses are logged; we can provide the audit log export as part of the SOC/GRC packet.

4) Residency: pilot — allow us to host in us-east for speed to pilot, with the contractual commitment that production will be EU-resident. Spinning an EU tenant typically takes 4–6 weeks and a one-time configuration fee (we’ll include numbers in the SOW).

5) Legal: we’ll add a short clause in the SOW called "ShortLog-72" recording the debug window, purge certificate, and access controls. That clause will be included in the initial template we send to OrbitHealth for review.

Attachments: privacy-summary.pdf (one-page), SOC2-snapshot.pdf (redacted snapshot).

Next steps I recommend:
- Sean/Laura: send the ShortLog-72 SOW clause + the two attachments to OrbitHealth for legal review.
- Laura: coordinate a short technical test plan (3-day debug-only run) so OrbitHealth can observe purge behavior.
- If OrbitHealth agrees, we will schedule the kickoff and prepare the EU-tenant timeline for production.

I can turn around the ShortLog-72 clause and a redline within 48 hours.

—Aditya Rao
Privacy & Security Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

--
Redwood Inference

From: Anna Morales <anna@orbithealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitHealth clarifications — recommended approach and proposed compromise

Thanks Aditya — that proposal is reasonable and addresses our main concerns. We are willing to accept the ShortLog-72 compromise for the pilot under these conditions: 

- Purge certificate: we need the purge confirmation (signed hash + timestamp) within 24 hours of the TTL job completing.
- Access approvals: OrbitHealth will provide a short allowlist (emails) for debug access; any Redwood ops access must be pre-authorized with justification and recorded in the audit export.
- Test plan: please provide the 3-day debug test plan and the SOW clause. Our legal & security teams will review the two attachments once received.

If you can get the clause + attachments over today/tomorrow, we’ll aim to have a redline back by Friday and target a pilot kickoff the week after.

Anna Morales
CTO, OrbitHealth

Attachments referenced: privacy summary (requested), SOC2 snapshot (requested)
snippet: OrbitHealth accepts ShortLog-72 compromise for pilot; asks for purge certificate within 24h, access allowlist, and 3-day test plan.
